fullPassage:
Whose Side Are You on?

Should social media have a "Dislike" button?

Charlie
One possible benefit of a "Dislike" button is that it would let people disagree with or be unhappy with a post without having to say something bad about it. This could help make conversations on social media platforms more open, honest, and respectful. A "Dislike" button could also help figure out what users like or find useful. By letting people express what they don't like about a post, content creators can get useful feedback and learn what their audience likes and doesn't like.

Jimin
The "Dislike" button can definitely be a useful tool to measure online engagement, but there are more negative effects than the positive. The presence of "Dislike" buttons and other negative replies illustrates how unfriendly social media can be. Many businesses directly ask for "5-star" ratings because anything less may actually hurt their reputation. A "Dislike" button encourages users to take advantage of the system rather than provide an honest opinion. While it may be useful for creators, it can also be harmful to both them and everyone else.

Is it okay to regift?

Lucia
Many gifts are thoughtful and personalized for the receiver. However, with online shopping apps and convenience stores everywhere, many gifts are also given just so that the giver isn't caught empty-handed. I don't see a problem with regifting common gifts until they find a home with someone who will appreciate them. The giving of the gift is the thoughtful gesture, not the actual gift itself. For this reason, you shouldn't feel guilty about regifting something that might be thrown away.

Richard
I don't think regifting is a good thing. A gift is something you receive from someone who put thought and effort into it. A gift is more than just an item. It contains the giver's feelings for the receiver. Something like that shouldn't just be given away to another person. Also, if the original giver finds out that their gift was given away, it could cause hard feelings. All in all, I don't think regifting is worth the trouble that it could cause. Just keep the gift as a reminder of a good relationship.

det.korean: 나쁜 말을 해야 할 필요 없이(without having to). have → having. 전치사 without 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② have → having: without + V-ing (전치사 + 동명사). without having to say = ~하지 않고도
❌ ① disagree: let people disagree (사역동사 let + 원형부정사) 정상
❌ ③ make: help make (help + 원형부정사) 정상
❌ ④ respectful: more open, honest, and respectful (병렬 형용사) 정상
det.tip: 전치사(without/about/of 등) + 동명사(-ing). without having to = ~하지 않고도

❌ ③ encourages: 주어 A button(단수) → 3인칭 단수 동사 정상
❌ ④ provide: rather than + 원형부정사 정상

det.korean: 선물을 주는 행위가 사려 깊은 행동이다.
det.analysis: The giving of the gift(주어: 선물을 주는 행위) + is(동사) + the thoughtful gesture(보어: 사려 깊은 행동)
det.tip: the giving of = ~을 주는 행위. 동명사(giving)가 주어로 쓰인 구문. 주어-동사-보어(S-V-C) 2형식

questions.passage: One possible benefit of a "Dislike" button is that it would let people disagree with or be unhappy with a post without having to say something bad about it. This could help make conversations on social media platforms more open, honest, and respectful. A "Dislike" button could also help figure out what users like or find useful. By letting people express what they don't like about a post, content creators can get useful feedback and learn what their audience likes and doesn't like.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 소셜 미디어의 '싫어요' 버튼은 대화를 건설적으로 만들고 콘텐츠 제작자에게 유용한 피드백을 제공할 수 있다.
소셜 미디어에서 부정적인 반응은 항상 해롭기 때문에 차단해야 한다.
'싫어요' 버튼은 사용자들 사이의 갈등을 심화시킬 뿐이다.
콘텐츠 제작자들은 사용자 피드백을 무시해야 한다.

det.korean: Charlie의 요지: '싫어요' 버튼이 대화를 건설적으로 만들고 제작자에게 유용한 피드백을 제공한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 건설적 대화 + 유용한 피드백: open/honest/respectful + useful feedback 두 핵심 근거
❌ ② 항상 해롭다: Charlie는 이점(benefit)을 설명하는 입장
❌ ③ 갈등 심화: 반대로 건설적 대화를 강조
❌ ④ 피드백 무시: 피드백을 얻는 것이 이점이라고 주장
det.tip: 핵심: more open, honest, respectful + useful feedback = '싫어요' 버튼의 긍정적 효과

questions.passage: Many gifts are thoughtful and personalized for the receiver. However, with online shopping apps and convenience stores everywhere, many gifts are also given just so that the giver isn't caught empty-handed. I don't see a problem with regifting common gifts until they find a home with someone who will appreciate them. The giving of the gift is the thoughtful gesture, not the actual gift itself. For this reason, you shouldn't feel guilty about regifting something that might be thrown away.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 모든 선물은 반드시 직접 만든 것이어야 한다.
흔한 선물의 재선물은 문제가 되지 않으며 죄책감을 느낄 필요가 없다.
온라인 쇼핑은 선물 문화를 완전히 파괴했다.
선물을 받으면 반드시 답례를 해야 한다.

det.korean: Lucia의 요지: 흔한 선물의 재선물은 문제없고, 죄책감을 느낄 필요 없다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 재선물 문제없음: 'I don't see a problem' + 'shouldn't feel guilty' 두 핵심 주장
❌ ① 직접 만든 선물: 원문에 없는 주장
❌ ③ 선물 문화 파괴: 극단적 주장. 원문은 재선물 찬성 입장
❌ ④ 답례 필수: 원문에 없는 내용
det.tip: 핵심: don't see a problem + shouldn't feel guilty = 재선물 찬성. gesture(행동)가 중요하지 물건이 아님

questions.passage: I don't think regifting is a good thing. A gift is something you receive from someone who put thought and effort into it. A gift is more than just an item. It contains the giver's feelings for the receiver. Something like that shouldn't just be given away to another person. Also, if the original giver finds out that their gift was given away, it could cause hard feelings. All in all, I don't think regifting is worth the trouble that it could cause. Just keep the gift as a reminder of a good relationship.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 원문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

"Richard는 재선물이 가져올 수 있는 문제만큼의 가치가 없다고 생각하며, 선물을 좋은 관계의 __________로 간직하라고 조언한다."

det.korean: 선물을 좋은 관계의 기념물(reminder)로 간직하라.
det.analysis: 원문 'keep the gift as a reminder of a good relationship'에서 reminder를 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: reminder = 기억나게 하는 것, 기념물. as a reminder of = ~의 기념물로서
